description: Published worked examples for the readability engine (COMM-01). Each case cites its source. Retrieved 2026-11-08.

smog_table.source: CDC. Simply Put: A Guide for Creating Easy-to-Understand Materials, 3rd ed. (July 2010), Appendix C, p. 31 (table developed by Harold C. McGraw, Baltimore County Schools). https://stacks.cdc.gov/view/cdc/11938/cdc_11938_DS1.pdf
smog_table.note: Simply Put misprints the 31-42 row as 61-42. 13 = 'college-level'. The table equals 3 + the square root of the nearest perfect square (McLaughlin 1969).

fry_short_document.source: CDC. Simply Put (July 2010), Appendix C, 'Using Fry on Short Documents', p. 34: hepatitis A example with fewer than 100 words.
fry_short_document.text:
Hepatitis A is a liver disease caused by the hepatitis A virus.

Hepatitis A can affect anyone in the United States. Hepatitis A can occur in situations ranging from isolated cases of disease to widespread epidemics.

Good personal hygiene and proper sanitation can help prevent hepatitis A. Vaccines are also available for long-term prevention of hepatitis A virus infection in persons 2 years of age and older. Immune globulin is available for short-term prevention of hepatitis A virus infection in all ages.
